_comment: Graph mirror of the fixed vocabulary declared in ontology/eip-governance.owl.
Loaded by scripts/ontology/LoadPersonaDomainProfile.java into the tenant's ArcadeDB.
Why it is duplicated at all: okg-reasoning-service reads the OWL and derives
closures into Fuseki, but the request-path services (nl-query, widgets,
graph-proxy) read ArcadeDB. RBAC has to be enforceable on the request path, so
the vocabulary needs a graph copy - exactly the arrangement EnterpriseSchemaBootstrap
already uses to mirror eip-enterprise.owl. Keep the two in step: every externalId
here is the local name of the corresponding OWL individual, lower-kebab-cased.
Classification is TYPE-level (one GovClassification row per graph type), which is
the faithful mirror of the class-level owl:hasValue restrictions. See the loader's
header for why per-row edges would be wrong.

sensitivityLevels.name: Restricted
sensitivityLevels.description: Held by NO persona. Exists so individual compensation, individual performance ratings and person-naming audit findings can be recognised and refused rather than served.

dataDomains.name: Enterprise
dataDomains.description: Company, mission, org structure, branches, clients, engagements.

dataDomains.name: Finance
dataDomains.description: Budgets, general ledger, cash flow, tax.

dataDomains.name: Treasury
dataDomains.description: Cash flow, liquidity, receivables and payables.

dataDomains.name: Payroll
dataDomains.description: Compensation cost. Aggregate only by design.

dataDomains.name: IT Spend
dataDomains.description: Deliberately a child of BOTH IT and Finance: the one slice of the ledger a CTO must see, reachable through the IT grant without opening the whole ledger.

dataDomains.name: Commercial
dataDomains.description: Pipeline, contracts, orders, revenue by client.

dataDomains.name: Strategy
dataDomains.description: Objectives, key results, initiatives, portfolio, decisions.

dataDomains.name: Portfolio
dataDomains.description: Programmes, projects, milestones and their RAG status.

dataDomains.name: Risk and Compliance
dataDomains.description: Risk register, controls, compliance obligations, audits.

dataDomains.name: Platform Governance
dataDomains.description: The platform's own configuration. NOT a parent of the business domains - administering the platform does not confer the right to read the company's numbers.

personas.name: Guest
personas.description: Signed in but not yet granted anything.

personas.name: Executive
personas.description: Generic senior leader; the floor every C-level persona builds on.

personas.name: CEO
personas._watchNote: Executive and finance focus: strategy (pending-decisions, objective-progress), portfolio (projects-at-risk), finance (budget-variance), treasury (net-cashflow), commercial (revenue-arr, pipeline-value) and risk (risk-exposure). IT and HR detail belong to the CTO and CHRO; critical items from those areas still reach the CEO through the escalation rule in PersonaDomainPolicy.
personas.description: Executive, finance, commercial and risk domains at Confidential - not technology or people detail, not Restricted and not Platform Governance. Mirrors the CEO scope in PersonaDomainPolicy. Embodied by the primary company leader - Zenitus is director-led with no single CEO title, so this mapping is a judgement call to confirm.

personas.name: CFO
personas.description: Whole finance tree, commercial, risk, plus Payroll specifically without the rest of HR. No embodiedBy: no CFO exists among this tenant's loaded executives, so OWN_* scopes fall back to tenant-wide for this persona.

personas.name: CTO
personas.description: Whole IT tree including IT Spend (a shared child of Finance) plus the delivery portfolio. No general ledger, payroll or pipeline.

personas.name: COO
personas.description: roleProvisioned=false: 'coo' is not in KeycloakProvisioningClient.REALM_ROLES, so no JWT can carry this persona yet.

personas.name: CHRO
personas.description: Whole HR tree at Confidential. Individual compensation still unreachable - that is Restricted and no persona holds it. roleProvisioned=false.

personas.name: Admin
personas.description: Configures the platform but holds NO business domain beyond Viewer. TIGHTENING of current behaviour: AccessPolicy.roleDefault() returns allow for every group when role == admin.

_newObservationsNote: Observations for the five new cross-domain widgets agree with the underlying rows in zenitus-domain-profile.json: pipeline = the 18.2M + 8.4M FY2027 Q2 snapshots; ARR = the active GID + VojVoj phase-2 contracts; risk exposure = residual exposure summed across the 6 open/mitigating risks; attrition = Quality FY2027 Q2 at 20%; objective progress = 2 of 6 key results at or past target.
_newWidgetsNote: The five widgets above close the domain gaps: before them NOTHING on the dashboard rendered Commercial, Contracts, Risk, Talent or Objective progress, so a CEO holding every domain still saw an IT-weighted board. Their values come from GovMetricObservation via /api/dashboard/persona-metrics/{widgetKey}, unlike the original 15 which read bespoke legacy endpoints.

metrics.name: Annual Payroll
metrics.description: An AGGREGATE only - never a per-person figure. Confidential rather than Restricted precisely because it is an aggregate.

_classificationsNote: The first block covers the 8000 IT-ops rows already loaded for this tenant. Classified by TYPE, so rows added later are covered automatically.

classifications.name: Cost Centre
classifications.description: eip:CostCentre and fin:CostCentre are owl:equivalentClass - one entity, two viewpoints.

classifications.name: Budget Item
classifications.description: IT budget lines are money, so they land in the shared IT/Finance child - visible to the CTO through IT and the CFO through Finance.

classifications.name: Vulnerability
classifications.description: An unpatched-vulnerability list is a target map, so it does not inherit the Internal sensitivity of the rest of the estate.

classifications.name: Work Item
classifications.description: Jira-sourced work items. Currently 0 rows, classified now so ingested data is covered on arrival rather than needing a backfill - the same reason classification is type-level.

classifications.name: Employee (legacy HR type)
classifications.description: The pre-existing HR vertex type that ArcadeDbContextBuilder.buildWorkforceContext summarises. Classified into Payroll/Confidential rather than Headcount/Internal because the type carries a PER-PERSON annualCtc property. NOTE: that property is exactly what eip-hr.owl says must not exist - individual compensation should live on hr:CompensationBand (a grade) or hr:PayrollRun (a population). The context builder only ever emits aggregates from it, so classifying it Confidential keeps the working feature while confining it to finance/people personas. Fixing the underlying type is a separate data-model change.

classifications.name: Monthly Cash Flow (legacy finance type)
classifications.description: The pre-existing finance vertex type. Aligned in eip-finance.owl as a subclass of fin:CashFlowEntry, so it inherits Treasury/Confidential in the OWL too - this row is the ArcadeDB mirror of that.

_accessGrantsNote: Tenant-editable overrides on top of the persona defaults. Kept minimal on purpose: the persona vocabulary should carry the policy, and grants should be the exception a tenant admin adds - not a second, competing copy of the matrix.

accessGrants.name: CTO portfolio scoped to own org subtree
accessGrants.description: The CTO sees portfolio data for their own org unit and everything beneath it, resolved through EMBODIED_BY then the ent:subUnitOf closure - rather than every project in the tenant.

accessGrants.name: Executive denied contract values
accessGrants.description: Explicit deny demonstrating that a grant can subtract as well as add: the generic Executive persona sees strategy but not commercial contract values.
